_conventions.default: untested. A field with no committed experiment that exercised it is untested with evidence []. Positional knowledge alone is not a label.
_conventions.evidence_ids: directory-name prefixes under experiments/ - this includes the RT-* red-team splice-and-observe experiments (A18 Pro), which are committed experiments with retained raw evidence, alongside EXP-NNNN and EXP-M4-NN / EXP-O2X.
_conventions.tokenization-only: used where the field's only established role is consuming bytes so the instruction length/framing round-trips; its evidence is the census / round-trip experiments (EXP-0036 A18 consolidation census, EXP-M4-12 residue closure, EXP-M4-13 full-corpus convergence) plus tools/agx-isa/roundtrip_test.py.
_conventions.corpus-correlation: used only where db.json or docs/ attributes the co-variation finding to a named experiment. EXP-M4-13 is COMPILE-ONLY (no dispatch), so nothing sourced from it can exceed this label.
_conventions.tested-but-unexplained: a field that WAS exercised on hardware but whose semantics remain unexplained is untested (semantics not established) with the observation recorded in `note`.
_conventions.target: per field, never assumed to transfer. EXP-0001..0046 and the RT-* passes and EXP-M4-14 ran on A18 Pro/G17P; EXP-0047+ and EXP-M4-01..M4-13 ran on M4/G16G. The EXP-0119 A18<->M4 contradiction is unresolved.
_conventions.emittable: an instruction qualifies only if EVERY field in its db.json descriptor is hardware-run or isolated-byte-diff (docs/evidence-classification.md section 2, the emittable rule). Field-less descriptors qualify only if the instruction itself is hardware-run / isolated-byte-diff.

opflags.label: hardware-run
opflags.range: each of bits 19..23 individually at {0,1}: 19=release srcA, 20=release srcB, 21=destination publication, 22/23=silent corrupt-to-zero
opflags.note: DISAGREEMENT, UNRESOLVED: EXP-0090 finding_1 established that a both-real falu2 REQUIRES opflags=3 (bit0+bit1) and that opflags=1 is a SILENT ZERO of the srcB read, falsified over 4 independent kernels. EXP-0112 then swept all 4 raw values in TWO shapes - including a byte-for-byte re-creation of EXP-0090's own falsifying construction - on a DIFFERENT carrier file and got the correct sum in all 8 runs, i.e. opflags had NO observable effect there. The release contract itself is separately established under two-run gates by EXP-0086/0089/0099/0119 across six families; the carrier dependence is not root-caused. Safe policy: emit opflags=3 for a both-real falu2 (correct under BOTH observations).

cache.range: byte+2 anchor 0x54 vs 0x56 tested at grid=1 and grid=4, with operand seeded from BOTH an ALU write and a device_load; additionally cache=0 vs cache=1 tested with srcdesc bit4 held at its retaining setting
cache.note: CONTRADICTION RESOLVED by EXP-0129 (commit 873cb9c3) - supersedes the earlier 'A18<->M4 contradiction, unresolved' label. The discriminator is the OPERAND'S PROVENANCE, not the device and not the dispatch shape: an ALU-seeded operand retains at grid=1 AND grid=4 with cache=1 AND cache=0 (8.4078e-45 in all four), while a device_load-seeded operand gives 2.8026e-45 at cache=1 and a silent 0.0 at cache=0, identically at grid=1 and grid=4. EXP-M4-14's own literal anchor bytes break at BOTH grid sizes. So EXP-M4-14 (A18) and EXP-0119 (M4) differed because they seeded operands differently; no device difference is implied and neither prior record was wrong. SEPARATELY: this `cache` bit is NOT ibitcount's release control. EXP-0129 located the real one at srcdesc bit4, and showed cache/bit17 stays independently inert even with bit4 at its retaining setting. Do not model `cache` as the retention flag.

Both falu2 signatures reproduce here: restore-on-rewrite (20.0 -> 28.0 when the register is rewritten before the later read) and distance-invariance (identical at 0, 1 and 4 intervening instructions). Supports ONE underlying release concept per family, not several unrelated mechanisms sharing a bit position.
